title: Integer Break
summary: Split n into at least two positive integer parts.

contractDetails.output-checking: Exact typed equality of the returned int.

statement: Split n into at least two positive integer parts. Return the largest possible product of the parts.

examples.explanation: A split of 3+4 reaches the maximum.
Use eighteen 3s and a final factor of 4.

hints: Conceptual: One big part can often be replaced with smaller factors that give a larger product.
Directional: Parts of size three are especially useful, but a final one wastes a factor.
Implementation: Take threes while the remainder exceeds four. Use the remaining two, three, or four as the final factor. Handle inputs below four separately.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space for iterative multiplication.
